proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(s,t\in\mathbb R\). By \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\), which is a member condition of \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\), \(p_x>0\), so the conditional channels are defined. From the definitions of the replicates,
\[
 e^{i(sS_1+tS_2)}=e^{i(s+t)A}e^{isU_1}e^{itU_2}.
\]
The joint independence in \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}latent\text{-}independence}\) and the coordinate independence in \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}coordinate\text{-}independence}\) therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 F_x(s,t)
 &=E_P[e^{i(s+t)A}\mid X=x]E_P[e^{isU_1}]E_P[e^{itU_2}]\\
 &=\left\{\int_{\mathcal A}e^{i(s+t)a}f_x(a)\,da\right\}\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\\
 &=\widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t).
\end{aligned}
\]
The same two independence assumptions allow the bounded mark to remain with the latent variables. Thus, using the definitions of \(m_x\) and \(q_x\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 G_x(s,t)
 &=E_P[Ye^{i(s+t)A}\mid X=x]E_P[e^{isU_1}]E_P[e^{itU_2}]\\
 &=\left\{\int_{\mathcal A}e^{i(s+t)a}E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]f_x(a)\,da\right\}\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\\
 &=\widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t).
\end{aligned}
\]
All expectations are finite: the probability-channel integrands have modulus one, while \(|Y|\le B_Y\) follows from \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcome}\), both member conditions of \(\mathcal M\). The support restriction used in the two displayed integrals is \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\). This proves both identities.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\). Positivity of \(p_x\) from \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) makes \(F_x\) and \(G_x\) functionals of the observed conditional law. Put
\[
 \delta=\min\left\{\frac{\nu_0}{2},\frac{1}{4B_A}\right\}>0.
\]
For \(|v|\le2\delta\), compact support of \(A\) and \(|e^{iz}-1|\le |z|\) for real \(z\) imply
\[
 |\widehat f_x(v)-1|
 \le \int_{\mathcal A}|e^{iva}-1|f_x(a)\,da
 \le B_A|v|\le\frac12.
\]
Consequently \(|\widehat f_x(v)|\ge1/2\) there. Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}local\text{-}modulus}\) also gives \(|\phi_j(v)|\ge c_0\) for \(|v|\le2\delta\). The identities in \(\mathrm{lem{:}factorization}\) therefore show that \(F_x(u,t)\ne0\) whenever \(|u|,|t|\le\delta\).

Since \(A\) is bounded by \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\) and \(E_P|U_2|<\infty\) follows from \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}moment}\) because \(q_e\ge8\), dominated differentiation is valid. Dividing the derivative of the first factorization identity by its nonzero value yields, for \(|u|\le\delta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_x(u)
 &:=\frac{\left.\partial_tF_x(u,t)\right|_{t=0}}{F_x(u,0)}\\
 &=\frac{\widehat f_x'(u)}{\widehat f_x(u)}+\frac{\phi_2'(0)}{\phi_2(0)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every quantity defining \(D_x\) is determined by the observed law. Characteristic-function normalization gives \(\phi_2(0)=1\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}center\text{-}two}\) gives
\[
 \phi_2'(0)=iE_P[U_2]=0.
\]
Hence
\[
 \widehat f_x'(u)=D_x(u)\widehat f_x(u),\qquad \widehat f_x(0)=1.
\]
If two laws in \(\mathcal M\) have the same observed law, their functions \(D_x\) coincide. For the ratio \(R(u)=\widehat f_x^{(1)}(u)/\widehat f_x^{(0)}(u)\) on \([-\delta,\delta]\), the preceding differential equation gives \(R'(u)=0\) and \(R(0)=1\). Thus the two latent transforms agree on this interval. Notice that no derivative of \(\phi_1\), and hence no location normalization on \(U_1\), entered this argument.

By \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\), for every complex \(z\),
\[
 |e^{iza}f_x(a)|\le e^{B_A|\operatorname{Im}z|}f_x(a).
\]
Dominated differentiation of every order therefore makes \(\widehat f_x\) entire. For the difference \(H\) of two candidate transforms, \(H(u)=0\) for real \(|u|<\delta\). Every real derivative of \(H\) at zero is consequently zero; complex differentiability makes these the complex derivatives, and the everywhere-convergent Taylor expansion
\[
 H(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{H^{(k)}(0)}{k!}z^k
\]
is therefore identically zero. Thus local equality extends to all of \(\mathbb C\) without requiring either error transform to be nonzero outside the protected neighborhood.

For the marked channel, the two factorizations at \((u,0)\), together with \(F_x(u,0)\ne0\), give the observed local formula
\[
 \widehat q_x(u)=\widehat f_x(u)\frac{G_x(u,0)}{F_x(u,0)},\qquad |u|\le\delta.
\]
Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcome}\) give \(|m_x|\le B_Y\) almost everywhere, whence \(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\) almost everywhere. Thus \(q_x\) is integrable and, by \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\), is supported on \(\mathcal A\). The same dominated-differentiation argument makes \(\widehat q_x\) entire, and the same Taylor-series argument extends its locally recovered value globally.

It remains to check that equality of these transforms identifies the functions rather than merely their transforms. If \(h\) is the difference of two candidate \(f_x\)'s, or of two candidate \(q_x\)'s, then \(h\in L^1(\mathbb R)\), is supported on \(\mathcal A\), and its Fourier transform vanishes on all of \(\mathbb R\). For \(\epsilon>0\), let
\[
 g_\epsilon(v)=(2\pi\epsilon)^{-1/2}e^{-v^2/(2\epsilon)}.
\]
The elementary Gaussian integral gives
\[
 g_\epsilon(v)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-itv}e^{-\epsilon t^2/2}\,dt.
\]
Fubini's theorem is applicable because \(h\in L^1\) and the Gaussian multiplier is integrable, and hence
\[
 (h*g_\epsilon)(a)
 =\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-ita}\widehat h(t)e^{-\epsilon t^2/2}\,dt=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \|h*g_\epsilon-h\|_1
 \le\int_{\mathbb R}g_\epsilon(v)\|h(\cdot-v)-h\|_1\,dv\longrightarrow0.
\]
The last limit follows by first checking translation continuity for compactly supported step functions and then approximating \(h\) in \(L^1\). Thus \(h=0\) almost everywhere. Finally, \(\beta>1/2\) gives unique continuous Sobolev representatives: by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat h(t)|\,dt
 \le \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^\beta|\widehat h(t)|^2\,dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2}<\infty,
\]
so Fourier inversion supplies a continuous representative, and two such representatives equal almost everywhere only if they equal everywhere. Hence the observed law uniquely determines every density \(f_x\) and every outcome-weighted density \(q_x\), including when an error characteristic function vanishes on an open set away from zero.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(a\in I\). By \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\), \(p_x>0\), so all conditional expectations below are well defined for this cell. Let \((\mathcal V,\mathscr V)\), \(V\), and \(h\) be supplied by \(\mathrm{ass{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}surface}\), and let
\[
 K_x(C)=P(V\in C\mid X=x),
 \qquad
 g_x(u)=\int_{\mathcal V}h(u,x,v)\,K_x(dv),
 \quad u\in\mathcal A.
\]
Joint measurability of \(h\) makes \(g_x\) measurable, and \(|h|\le B_Y\) makes every integral finite. The simultaneous probability-one equality in \(\mathrm{ass{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}surface}\), evaluated at the random coordinate \(A\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) give
\[
 Y=Y(A)=h(A,X,V)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
For every bounded Borel function \(\psi:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R\), conditional independence \(V\perp A\mid X\) from \(\mathrm{ass{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}surface}\) and the definition of the conditional density \(f_x\) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\!\left[Y\psi(A)\mid X=x\right]
 &=E_P\!\left[h(A,x,V)\psi(A)\mid X=x\right]\\
 &=\int_{\mathcal A}\int_{\mathcal V}
       h(u,x,v)\psi(u)\,K_x(dv)f_x(u)\,du\\
 &=\int_{\mathcal A}g_x(u)\psi(u)f_x(u)\,du.
\end{aligned}
\]
On the other hand, the defining property of the conditional regression \(m_x(u)=E_P[Y\mid A=u,X=x]\) implies
\[
 E_P\!\left[Y\psi(A)\mid X=x\right]
 =\int_{\mathcal A}m_x(u)\psi(u)f_x(u)\,du.
\]
Uniqueness of Radon--Nikodym derivatives therefore gives
\[
 m_x(u)=g_x(u)
 \quad\text{for }f_x(u)\,du\text{-almost every }u\in\mathcal A.
\]

We next remove this almost-everywhere qualification on \(I\). By \(\mathrm{ass{:}f\text{-}sobolev}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}q\text{-}sobolev}\), and \(\beta>3/2\), each of \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) has a continuous representative. Indeed, for either function \(w\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat w(t)|\,dt
 \le
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^{\beta}|\widehat w(t)|^2\,dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2}<\infty.
\]
Thus its inverse Fourier integral is continuous by dominated convergence and equals \(w\) almost everywhere by Fourier inversion. We use these continuous representatives. Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}denominator}\) gives \(f_x(u)\ge\kappa>0\) on \(I\), so
\[
 \widetilde m_x(u):=\frac{q_x(u)}{f_x(u)},\qquad u\in I,
\]
is continuous. Since \(q_x=m_xf_x\) by the definition of \(q_x\), the preceding almost-everywhere equality implies
\[
 \widetilde m_x(u)=g_x(u)
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }u\in I;
\]
the passage from \(f_x(u)\,du\)-null sets to Lebesgue-null sets uses \(f_x\ge\kappa\). The map \(g_x\) is continuous on \(I\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}causal\text{-}mean\text{-}continuity}\), because the structural representation gives
\[
 g_x(u)=E_P[Y(u)\mid X=x].
\]
Two continuous functions on the interval \(I\) that agree Lebesgue-almost everywhere agree everywhere: otherwise continuity would produce a nonempty relative open subinterval on which their difference is bounded away from zero, contradicting almost-everywhere equality. Hence, for every \(u\in I\),
\[
 E_P[Y(u)\mid X=x]=g_x(u)=\widetilde m_x(u)=\frac{q_x(u)}{f_x(u)}.
\]

Because \(\mathcal X\) is finite, the law of total expectation now gives, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mu(a)
 &=E_P[Y(a)] &&\text{by the definition of \(\mu\)}\\
 &=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xE_P[Y(a)\mid X=x]
    &&\text{by conditioning on the finite partition generated by \(X\)}\\
 &=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}
    &&\text{by the pointwise bridge proved above}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the relationship between the causal target and the regression functional; it has not been imposed as a definition. Finally, \(p_x\) is the observed marginal probability of \(X=x\), while \(\mathrm{thm{:}marked\text{-}cocycle\text{-}id}\) makes every \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) a functional of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\). Division is legitimate on \(I\) by \(f_x\ge\kappa\), so the displayed causal curve is point identified from \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

The structural condition is compatible with the fixed-nuisance common-uniform Bernoulli lower construction. Given continuous conditional means \(b_{j,n,x}:\mathcal A\to[1/4,3/4]\), take a single \(V\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) independent of \((A,X,U_1,U_2)\), and put
\[
 h_{j,n}(u,x,v)=\mathbf 1\{v\le b_{j,n,x}(u)\},
 \qquad
 Y_{j,n}(u)=h_{j,n}(u,X,V).
\]
Then \(h_{j,n}\) is jointly measurable, \(V\perp A\mid X\), consistency holds after setting \(Y_{j,n}=Y_{j,n}(A)\), and
\[
 E[Y_{j,n}(u)\mid X=x]=b_{j,n,x}(u),
\]
which is continuous. Since \(B_Y\ge1\), these schedules also obey the frozen outcome bound, and no measurement-error condition is changed.

Let \(m=|\mathcal X|\) and
\[
 \epsilon_n=\left\{\frac{\log(6m/\alpha)}{2n}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
For each \(x\), \(\widehat p_x\) is the average of \(n\) independent Bernoulli variables by \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\). If \(Z\in[0,1]\), exponential tilting and two integrations of the second-derivative bound for the log moment-generating function give
\[
 \log E[e^{\lambda(Z-EZ)}]\le\frac{\lambda^2}{8},\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R.
\]
Indeed, the second derivative is the variance of a tilted variable in \([0,1]\), which is at most \(1/4\), while the value and first derivative at zero are zero. Exponential Markov, independence, and optimization at \(\lambda=4\epsilon_n\) for the upper tail and \(\lambda=-4\epsilon_n\) for the lower tail therefore give
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(|\widehat p_x-p_x|>\epsilon_n)
 \le2e^{-2n\epsilon_n^2}=\frac{\alpha}{3m}.
\]
The union bound over the finite set \(\mathcal X\) therefore gives
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\left(\max_x|\widehat p_x-p_x|\le\epsilon_n\right)\ge1-\frac\alpha3.
\]
Because the true mass vector is nonnegative and sums to one, the event in parentheses is exactly its membership in \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), by \(\mathrm{def{:}mass\text{-}confidence\text{-}region}\). The displayed coordinate bound is part of the same definition.

For the count claim, if \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,p)\), exponential Markov applied to \(e^{-tN}\), followed by \(1-p+pe^{-t}\le\exp\{p(e^{-t}-1)\}\), gives
\[
 P(N\le np/2)\le\inf_{t>0}\exp\{tnp/2+np(e^{-t}-1)\}.
\]
Choosing \(t=\log2\) makes the exponent \(-np(1-\log2)/2\le-np/8\). Therefore, for \(n_x\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,p_x)\),
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(n_x<np_x/2)\le e^{-np_x/8}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) has \(p_x\ge p_{\min}\); moreover, \(n_x<np_{\min}/2\) implies \(n_x<np_x/2\). Another union bound consequently yields
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\left(\min_xn_x<np_{\min}/2\right)
 \le\sum_xe^{-np_x/8}
 \le m e^{-np_{\min}/8}.
\]

Finally, let \(p\) and \(p'\) be two mass vectors in the confidence region while \((f_x,q_x)\) is fixed and feasible. Feasibility in \(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\), or bounded outcomes for a model member, gives \(|q_x(a)/f_x(a)|\le B_Y\) wherever the quotient is used. Hence, uniformly over \(a\in I\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left|\sum_x(p_x-p_x')\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|
 &\le B_Y\sum_x|p_x-p_x'|\\
 &\le2B_Ym\epsilon_n.
\end{aligned}
\]
Writing \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>1\),
\[
 \frac{\epsilon_n}{r_n}
 =O\left(n^{-1/2}\left\{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right\}^{\gamma}\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
This proves the claimed profiling contribution and all three probability bounds.

Suppose \(Y(a)=1\) almost surely for every \(a\in\mathcal A\). Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) gives \(Y=1\) almost surely, and therefore \(m_x(a)=1\) for \(f_x(a)\,da\)-almost every \(a\). Hence
\[
 q_x(a)=m_x(a)f_x(a)=f_x(a)
\]
almost everywhere. Since \(f_x,q_x\in H^\beta(\mathbb R)\) and \(\beta>3/2\), their continuous Sobolev representatives coincide everywhere. The two definitions of the observable channels now give, for all \(s,t\),
\[
 G_x(s,t)=E[Ye^{i(sS_1+tS_2)}\mid X=x]
 =E[e^{i(sS_1+tS_2)}\mid X=x]=F_x(s,t),
\]
and the causal definition gives \(\mu(a)=E[Y(a)]=1\).

The cited \(\mathrm{lem{:}capitao\text{-}theorem\text{-}one}\) applies to the probability channel: compact support of \(A\) in \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\) implies its condition (H2), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}coordinate\text{-}independence}\) is its condition (H1). That theorem identifies the latent and error laws up to their common translation. In the present scalar model, \(E_P[U_2]=0\) from \(\mathrm{ass{:}center\text{-}two}\) fixes this translation, exactly as the derivative calculation in \(\mathrm{thm{:}marked\text{-}cocycle\text{-}id}\) shows. Thus, after deleting the now redundant marked channel \(G_x=F_x\), the probability-channel argument is the stated normalized special case of their Theorem 1.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The constrained-sieve embedding and the quantitative discrete analytic-cocycle modulus at order \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) remain unproved.
open_obligations.obstruction: Local qualitative identifiability supplies no uniform singular-value estimate. The frozen construction supplies neither a proved stability inequality for the bilinear grid map with two unknown atomic error factors nor a shape-preserving Jackson operator that simultaneously preserves normalization, the lower bound on \(I\), both Sobolev-radius constraints, and \(|q|\le B_Yf\).
open_obligations.attempted: The simultaneous empirical-transform event and global clipping bound were proved. Direct interpolation was then tested, but it neither controls the unknown error factors in the discrete bilinear cocycle nor preserves the nonlinear density and marked-sieve constraints.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The simultaneous confidence event and clipping assertions are proved. Conditional on the cell labels, each probability-channel summand has modulus at most one and each marked-channel summand has modulus at most \(B_Y\). Applying the real bounded-variable exponential inequality to real and imaginary parts gives, when \(n_x>\lambda_n\),
\[
 P\left(\left.|\widehat F_{x,n}(s,t)-F_x(s,t)|
 >2\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\,\right|\,(X_i)_{i=1}^n\right)
 \le4e^{-\lambda_n},
\]
and the analogous inequality for \(\widehat G_{x,n}\) with radius \(2B_Y\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\). When \(n_x\le\lambda_n\), the deterministic bounds \(|\widehat F_{x,n}-F_x|\le2\) and \(|\widehat G_{x,n}-G_x|\le2B_Y\) apply. A union bound over the two channels, all \(x\in\mathcal X\), and all \((s,t)\in\mathcal D_n\) costs at most
\[
 8|\mathcal X||\mathcal D_n|e^{-\lambda_n}=\alpha/6.
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\), this proves the claimed weaker bound \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha\). Also, every feasible \(\mu_\theta\) lies in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\), and the endpoint rule therefore gives \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), including the empty-set convention. What remains unproved is the constrained-sieve embedding and the deterministic inverse estimate
\[
 \sup_{\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}
 \|\mu_\theta-\mu_{\theta'}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \lesssim K_n^{1/2-\beta}+\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}.
\]

open_obligations.what_is_open: The upper theorem now has its pointwise causal bridge, but it still requires the feasible constrained-sieve embedding and the deterministic analytic stability bound from \(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\).
open_obligations.obstruction: Without those deterministic assertions, the true approximating tuple is not known to belong to \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), and empirical residual control cannot bound the diameter of the profiled ADRF set. Thus neither uniform coverage of the stated construction nor its \(r_n\) width follows yet.
open_obligations.attempted: The coverage and expected-width reduction was completed conditional on feasible embedding and the inverse modulus, including the regular-count split, the \(o(r_n)\) multinomial term, and the exponentially small count-failure remainder.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The causal bridge needed for coverage is supplied by \(\mathrm{thm{:}adrf\text{-}id}\). Conditional on the two unresolved deterministic assertions in \(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\), the rest of the upper theorem follows. On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), a feasible approximating tuple \(\bar\theta\) satisfying \(\|\mu_{\bar\theta}-\mu\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le b_{\mu,n}\) and the profiled endpoint definitions imply \(L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\). On the regular-count event, the deterministic feasible-set diameter and the two endpoint inflations give
\[
 W_n\le C\left\{K_n^{1/2-\beta}+\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}\right\}\le C'r_n,
\]
because \(b_{\mu,n}=O(K_n^{1/2-\beta})\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}=o(r_n)\). On count failure, \(W_n\le2B_Y\), while \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\) bounds its probability by \(|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}\). Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]
 \le C'r_n+2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}
 =O(r_n).
\]
Thus the remaining obstruction is deterministic analytic stability and feasible sieve embedding, not causal identification or an additional probabilistic argument.

proofs.proof_tex:
Assume the affirmative content of \(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\).  Thus there are constants \(\eta\in(0,1-2\alpha)\), \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\), and an integer \(n_0\) such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\), the two laws \(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}\) belong to \(\mathcal M\) and satisfy
\[
 Q_{j,n}:=((P_{j,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},\qquad
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{0,n},Q_{1,n})\le \eta,
 \qquad
 \Delta_n:=\|\mu_{1,n}-\mu_{0,n}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \ge c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}.
\]
Fix \(n\ge n_0\) and an arbitrary band \(\mathcal C_n=(L_n,U_n)\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\).  For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), define the measurable simultaneous-coverage event
\[
 H_{j,n}:=\{L_n(a)\le \mu_{j,n}(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}.
\]
Because \(P_{j,n}\in\mathcal M\), uniform honesty in \(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\) gives
\[
 Q_{j,n}(H_{j,n})\ge 1-\alpha,
 \qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
By the defining event inequality for total variation, \(Q_{0,n}(E)\ge Q_{1,n}(E)-\operatorname{TV}(Q_{0,n},Q_{1,n})\) for every measurable event \(E\).  Taking \(E=H_{1,n}\) and using the displayed total-variation bound yields
\[
 Q_{0,n}(H_{1,n})\ge 1-\alpha-\eta.
\]
The union bound under \(Q_{0,n}\) therefore gives
\[
 Q_{0,n}(H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n})
 \ge Q_{0,n}(H_{0,n})+Q_{0,n}(H_{1,n})-1
 \ge 1-2\alpha-\eta.
\]
On \(H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n}\), for every \(a\in I\), the interval \([L_n(a),U_n(a)]\) contains both \(\mu_{0,n}(a)\) and \(\mu_{1,n}(a)\).  Hence
\[
 U_n(a)-L_n(a)\ge |\mu_{1,n}(a)-\mu_{0,n}(a)|
\]
for every \(a\in I\), and taking suprema gives \(W_n\ge\Delta_n\) on that event.  Since \(W_n\ge0\) almost surely by \(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{Q_{0,n}}[W_n]
 &\ge E_{Q_{0,n}}[W_n\mathbf 1\{H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n}\}]\\
 &\ge \Delta_n Q_{0,n}(H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n})\\
 &\ge (1-2\alpha-\eta)c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The law \(P_{0,n}\) is one member of \(\mathcal M\), so, for this arbitrary honest band,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]
 \ge E_{Q_{0,n}}[W_n]
 \ge c'K_n^{1/2-\beta},
 \qquad
 c':=(1-2\alpha-\eta)c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0,
\]
where strict positivity follows from \(\eta<1-2\alpha\) and \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\).  Taking the infimum over \(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\) proves the asserted all-honest-band lower bound.

It remains only to compare the deterministic scales.  Put \(\gamma:=\beta-1/2>0\), using \(\beta>3/2\), and \(x_n:=\log n/\log\log n\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(x_n\ge2\), and the definition \(K_n=\lfloor x_n\rfloor\) implies
\[
 \frac{x_n}{2}\le K_n\le x_n.
\]
Because \(1/2-\beta=-\gamma\),
\[
 x_n^{-\gamma}\le K_n^{-\gamma}\le 2^\gamma x_n^{-\gamma}.
\]
Finally \(x_n^{-\gamma}=(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}=r_n\).  Therefore \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\asymp r_n\), with constants depending only on \(\beta\), which completes the proof.
